title: Observed angle sums of survey triangles: Schott (USC&GS SP 4 and 7), Delambre & Méchain, Maclear, Roy, Struve; our transcription
verdict_rule: Observed angle sums that stay at 180° whatever the size of the triangle, or an excess that does not grow with the area (a constant offset fitting as well as the line through zero).

sources.cite: C. A. Schott, The Transcontinental Triangulation and the American Arc of the Parallel, U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey Special Publication No. 4 (Washington, 1900): triangles of the base nets and adjusted triangles of the main triangulation; resulting geographic positions

C. A. Schott, The Eastern Oblique Arc of the United States and Osculating Spheroid, U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey Special Publication No. 7 (Washington, 1902): resulting angles and sides; synopsis of the base lines (p. 100); resulting geographic positions

J.-B. Delambre and P. Méchain, Base du système métrique décimal (Paris, 1806-1810): t. 1 pp. 513-542 (Tableau général des triangles), t. 2 p. 56 (the bases) and pp. 800-841 (Tableau complet des triangles), t. 3 Table V (positions); ETH-Bibliothek Zürich copy
T. Maclear, Verification and Extension of La Caille's Arc of Meridian at the Cape of Good Hope (London, 1866), pp. 533-558 (principal and secondary triangles) and 589 (positions); Cornell copy

W. Roy, An account of the trigonometrical operation whereby the distance between the meridians of the Royal Observatories of Greenwich and Paris has been determined, Phil. Trans. 80 (1790) 111-270, pp. 64-79 of the offprint (calculation of the triangles)
F. G. W. Struve, Arc du méridien de 25° 20′ entre le Danube et la mer Glaciale, vol. 1 (St Petersburg, 1860): p. 76 (the six bases), tableaux A (pp. 96-102), C, D, E (pp. 111-143)

units.deg, min, sec: observed angle as printed (sec may print 60 or more, as in the sources)
units.corr, sph, exc: printed correction, spherical-angle seconds and spherical excess, arcseconds (used only to check the transcription)
units.log, dist: printed log10 of the side and the side in metres (used only to check the transcription and to find ambiguous station pairs)
units.lat, lon: printed positions, degrees minutes seconds on the Clarke 1866 spheroid, longitude WEST positive (drawing only)
units.flag: a misprint of the source verified on the page image; the triangle is left out of the fit and counted
units.dist: side opposite the station as printed: metres (Schott), toises of 1.949036591 m (Delambre, Struve), English feet of 0.3048 m (Maclear, Roy)
units.adj_sec: generic format (Roy, Maclear, Struve): seconds of the printed adjusted plane angle (checks only)

inputs.origin: The printed tables of Schott (USC&GS SP 4, 1900, and SP 7, 1902), Delambre & Méchain, Maclear, Roy and Struve (pages named in the file name and in the sources), read off the page images by Sonnet subagents, one line per printed angle.
inputs.checks: research/surv_excess_check.py, then the build: observed + correction = spherical, triangle closure, log/distance, sine rule; the build fails on a disagreement that is not flagged.
inputs.caveats: A misread digit in an angle that no check covers could pass; flagged rows say why they are kept.

notes: Every row was read off the page images (the PDFs' OCR is unusable) by Sonnet subagents and checked by research/surv_excess_check.py and by the build (observed+correction=spherical, closure, log/distance, sine rule; positions against the printed sides on Clarke 1866). Areas come from the measured bases through the observed angles only; the bases are printed reduced to sea level, the one place a radius enters (~1e-6 of the lengths). Delambre, Maclear, Roy and Struve (2026-10-28): same rules; a triangle whose only fault is a misprinted side keeps its angles (sides are not used); a concluded or misprinted angle can still carry lengths as 180° minus the two others, never entering the fit; sides two triangles imply through a shared ray (quadrilaterals, Roy) are closed by the law of cosines. Roy's 1790 angles cannot resolve the excess on his small triangles (shown, bound only).
